ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in rectangle $ABCD$, it is known that $AB=8\,cm$, $BC=10\,cm$. Fold $AD$ along the straight line $AE$, making point D land on point F which is on side $BC$. What is the length of $CF$ in $cm$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In the rectangle $ABCD$, \\
$\because$ $AB=8\text{cm}$, $BC=10\text{cm}$, let $CF=x\text{cm}$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD=BC=10\text{cm}$, $BF=(10-x)\text{cm}$, $\angle B=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ folding $AD$ along the line $AE$, such that point $D$ falls on point $F$ on side $BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADE \cong \triangle AFE$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD=AF=10\text{cm}$, \\
In $\triangle ABF$, by the Pythagorean theorem, $AB^2+BF^2=AF^2$, \\
$\therefore$ $8^2+(10-x)^2=10^2$, solving for $x$, we find $x=\boxed{4}$, \\
$\therefore$ $CF=4\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; point E is on the right side CD, point F is on the lower side BC; dashed lines AE, AF, EF are drawn in the figure, indicating the corresponding line segment relationship after folding. Reasoning: In rectangle ABCD, it is known that AB=8 cm, BC=10 cm, so AD=BC=10 cm, and AB is perpendicular to BC. When folding, point A on the crease AE remains fixed, and point D falls onto point F; therefore folding preserves length, AD corresponds to AF, so AF=AD=10 cm. Let CF=x cm, then BF=BC-CF=10-x. Since F is on BC, triangle ABF is right-angled at B; applying the Pythagorean theorem: AB^2+BF^2=AF^2, that is, 8^2+(10-x)^2=10^2. Thus (10-x)^2=36, and BF=10-x is positive, giving 10-x=6, so x=4. Therefore CF=4 cm.
